title: Take the steel and electronic items off a patient cart's tray before it goes into the MRI scanner room
instruction: Make this cart safe for the MRI scanner room: put anything that must stay out into the grey bin; leave everything else on the cart.
context: MRI technologists and nurses screen every patient cart before it enters the magnet room (Zone IV), because the magnet pulls ferromagnetic objects in as projectiles and heats or wipes electronics; scissors, penlights, phones and stethoscopes are the routine finds. In 2001 an oxygen cylinder carried into a scanner room killed a six-year-old (Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert 38; ACR Manual on MR Safety). The check is repeated for every scan. Typical misses are an item under a positioning pad and a stethoscope left lying across the bedding; the opposite error is stripping the cart of MR-safe things the patient needs. Nothing in the instruction says which objects are hazards. The physical work is the hard part: thin flat steel must be pinched off a tray floor, a pad lifted away to free the phone beneath it, and a limp 0.7 m stethoscope with a heavy end lifted off light foam items without dragging them along, then fed whole into a bin, which takes both hands.
setup:
Metres from the midpoint between the arm bases (bases at y = +/-0.305); x forward, y left, z up from the table top. All items real size; long axes along y unless stated. Hazard status follows from material, stated per item.
FIXED (clamped). (1) Cart-top tray, green ABS (MR-safe): inside 0.260 (x) by 0.720 (y), x 0.140 to 0.400, y -0.360 to 0.360; 3 mm floor and walls, rim 25 mm above the floor. (2) Bin, grey polypropylene: outside 0.150 (x) by 0.350 (y) by 0.080 high, x -0.020 to 0.130, y -0.175 to 0.175; 3 mm walls and floor; empty.
HAZARDS (loose, on the tray floor). (3) Lister bandage scissors, 7.25 in (184 mm), 420 stainless steel (ferromagnetic), closed, lying flat, 5 mm thick: two finger rings 28 mm across at the +y end, shanks, pivot screw, blades angled 30 deg toward +x with a blunt probe tip; 105 g; middle of its length at (0.185, 0.170). (4) Penlight, 150 mm long: 13 mm blue anodised aluminium barrel, 15 mm steel head (lamp at +y), steel tail cap and steel pocket clip (46 mm, on the +x side, touching the tray), two AAA cells inside (ferromagnetic clip and cells); 45 g; centre (0.320, 0.190). (5) Smartphone in a black TPU case, 150.4 x 74.4 x 10.6 mm, 200 g (electronic, with magnets and a battery), screen down, camera island (36 mm square, 1.6 mm proud, two lenses) at the -y end; centre (0.250, -0.267); covered by pad (7) except the last 12 mm at the -y end. (6) Stethoscope, dual-head, 0.70 m overall, 160 g: stainless steel chestpiece 45 mm across and 22 mm thick with a 20 mm stem (ferromagnetic), 440 mm of 10 mm burgundy PVC tubing, and a headset 176 mm long (PVC yoke, two 6 mm metal ear tubes 60 mm apart with spring steel inside, soft ear tips). Chestpiece flat on the tray at (0.281, 0.322); the tubing runs toward -y along the tray floor through (0.268, 0.18) and (0.250, 0.02), climbs the wedge (8), bridges to the pad (7) at 50 mm height, and the headset lies on top of the pad: yoke at (0.250, -0.150), ear tips at (0.250 +/-0.027, -0.320).
MR-SAFE (loose). (7) Blue polyurethane-foam positioning pad 190 x 80 x 30 mm, 25 g (55 kg/m3), centre (0.250, -0.235), lying on the phone. (8) Grey polyurethane-foam positioning wedge 120 (y) x 80 (x) x 40 mm, 11 g, a ramp rising from 0 at y = 0.000 to 40 mm at y = -0.120, centre (0.250, -0.060), on the tray floor. (9) Closed PET water bottle, 0.33 L, 60 mm diameter, 165 mm tall, full, 350 g, upright at (0.360, 0.050).
Friction (static/dynamic): steel, aluminium and PET on ABS 0.4/0.3; phone case 0.5/0.4; foam 0.8/0.7; tubing 0.5/0.4. Tubing: limp, bends to a 40 mm radius, holds no shape. Grippers start open at the ready pose. Full dimension table in the README.
scoring:
Hazards: scissors, penlight, phone, stethoscope. MR-safe items: pad, wedge, bottle.
In the bin (scissors, penlight, phone): the item's centre (centre of its bounding box) is inside the bin's inner walls, above its floor and below its rim.
Stethoscope in the bin: the centre of the chestpiece, the yoke, the middle of both ear tubes and both ear tips are all inside the bin's inner walls and below its rim. The tubing may lie in the bin, arch above its rim, or hang over the rim outside the bin, but no part of the tubing outside the bin's outer walls may be over the tray (seen from above) or within 10 mm of the table: the whole stethoscope must be off the cart and not trailing on the table.
Kept on the cart (pad, wedge, bottle): centre inside the tray's inner walls, resting on the tray floor or on another item on the tray; the bottle within 20 deg of upright. They may be moved or lifted along the way.
Released and at rest: each gripper's centre point between the pads is at least 30 mm from the item's bounding box, and no point on the item moves 0.5 mm or more between 20 Hz steps (under 1 cm/s; checked on the corners of each rigid item's outline box and, for the stethoscope, on the chestpiece, headset and every tube joint), held for 1 s.
Score = 0.2 for each hazard in the bin, released and at rest (0 to 0.8), plus 0.2 when all four hazards count and all three MR-safe items are kept on the cart, released and at rest. So: 0 doing nothing; 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 for one to three hazards; 0.8 for all four with the bottle toppled or an MR-safe item still held; 1.0 for everything, held 1 s (success). A hazard left on the tray, dropped on the table, hovering or still gripped earns nothing.
Score 0 at the end if (a) a pad, wedge or bottle is in the bin (centre inside the inner walls with its lowest point below the rim) or (b) a pad, wedge or bottle is off the cart (centre outside the tray's inner walls with its lowest point below the tray rim's top: fallen or set down off the tray). An MR-safe item taken back out of the bin or returned to the tray before the end does not count against the trial.
Real trial: video the run; after release and 1 s of stillness photograph bin and tray from above and the side. With a ruler check each hazard's centre is inside the bin walls below the rim, no tubing lies over the tray or touches the table, the three MR-safe items stand inside the tray rim, and none is in the bin or off the cart.
run_limit: 3,000 steps (2.5 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted demo takes about 1,300 steps
reset_notes: Empty the bin. Put the phone screen down at its mark and lay the pad on it so 12 mm of the phone's camera end shows; set the wedge at its mark with the high end toward the pad. Lay the stethoscope last: chestpiece flat on the tray, tubing up the wedge, headset on top of the pad. Place scissors (closed) and penlight flat at their marks, stand the capped bottle upright. Tray and bin stay clamped.
fidelity: Only the tray stands in for the cart top (a real stretcher is about 0.7 x 2 m and rolls). No magnetic field is simulated: hazard status comes from each item's material. All items are real size and rigid except the tubing: foam pad and wedge are rigid solids, the bottle a solid of its filled mass, the scissors do not open, the headset's spring and yoke are rigid, the tubing is 22 hinged 20 mm capsules. Finger rings collide as discs. Stethoscope part masses are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (no object moved; the run stopped at the 1-hour wall-clock limit after 2,808 of 3,000 steps); demo: 1.0
